deep.reconstruction:
Context: this sheet matches p. 336 of Ramanujan's 'lost notebook'. The preceding sheet (lost notebook p. 335) gives Bessel-series formulas for sums of the form sum [x/n] sin(2 pi n theta), i.e. the same circle of ideas as the divisor problem. Here sigma_s(n) = sum over d|n of d^s.

(A) The modular-type claim, the key underlying statement. Define
F(a) = zeta(1-s)/a + (1/2) zeta(-s) tan(pi s/2) + sum_{n>=1} sigma_s(n) sin(n a).
Ramanujan asserts: if a*b = 4 pi^2, then a^{(s+1)/2} F(a) = b^{(s+1)/2} F(b).

(B) The first displayed identity is the Laplace transform of (A). Reconstruction (mine; the computation is not on the page):
- For Re(x) > 0: Gamma(s+1/2) (x - i n)^{-s-1/2} = int_0^oo t^{s-1/2} e^{-(x - i n) t} dt.
- Hence Gamma(s+1/2) [(x-in)^{-s-1/2} - (x+in)^{-s-1/2}]/(2i) = int_0^oo t^{s-1/2} e^{-xt} sin(nt) dt.
- Also Gamma(s+1/2)/((s-1/2) x^{s-1/2}) = Gamma(s-1/2) x^{1/2-s} = int_0^oo t^{s-3/2} e^{-xt} dt.
- And Gamma(s+1/2) x^{-s-1/2} = int_0^oo t^{s-1/2} e^{-xt} dt.
- So the left side of the first identity is, formally, int_0^oo t^{s-1/2} e^{-xt} F(t) dt.

Now substitute (A) with b = 4 pi^2/t:
t^{s-1/2} F(t) = (2 pi)^{s+1} t^{-3/2} F(4 pi^2/t).
Integrate term by term:
- Term zeta(1-s) t/(4 pi^2): this gives (2 pi)^{s+1} zeta(1-s) sqrt(pi/x)/(4 pi^2) = (2 pi)^s zeta(1-s)/(2 sqrt(pi x)).
- Constant term: int_0^oo t^{-3/2} e^{-xt} dt is divergent at 0. Read as Gamma(-1/2) x^{1/2} = -2 sqrt(pi x), it gives -(2 pi)^s 2 pi sqrt(pi x) zeta(-s) tan(pi s/2).
- Series term: use int_0^oo t^{-3/2} e^{-xt} sin(c/t) dt = sqrt(pi/c) e^{-sqrt(2cx)} sin(pi/4 + sqrt(2cx)), with c = 4 pi^2 n. This follows from int t^{-3/2} e^{-pt - q/t} dt = sqrt(pi/q) e^{-2 sqrt(pq)} with q = -ic. It gives (2 pi)^s sqrt(pi) sigma_s(n) n^{-1/2} e^{-2 pi sqrt(2 n x)} sin(pi/4 + 2 pi sqrt(2 n x)).

This reproduces the right side on the page exactly. So the page records the (false) transformation (A) together with its formal Laplace-transform consequence (B). The aim is evidently a Voronoi-type expansion for sums of sigma_s(n), i.e. the extended divisor problem.
errors: The series sum sigma_s(n) sin(n a) in (A) diverges for every real a: sigma_s(n) >= 1, so its terms do not tend to 0. Identity (A) is therefore meaningless as stated. Berndt-Dixit-Roy-Zaharescu (2017) show the page-336 claims are vitiated by divergent series and incorrect as stated.

The series on the left of the first identity also diverges, for generic s. For large n, the bracket/(2i) is about n^{-s-1/2} sin(pi(2s+1)/4), so the terms are of size sigma_{-s}(n) n^{-1/2} >= n^{-1/2}.
Only the right-hand series converges, thanks to the factor exp(-2 pi sqrt(2 n x)).

The constant term rests on the divergent integral int_0^oo t^{-3/2} e^{-xt} dt, which was evaluated by analytic continuation as Gamma(-1/2) sqrt(x). Termwise integration of a divergent series is also unjustified.
The formula degenerates at odd positive integer s, where tan(pi s/2) has a pole while zeta(-s) is nonzero.

results.what: Claimed transformation: a^{(s+1)/2}{zeta(1-s)/a + zeta(-s) tan(pi s/2)/2 + sum sigma_s(n) sin(n a)} is invariant under a -> 4 pi^2/a.
results.modern_name: Modular-type (Eisenstein-series-type) transformation for sums of sigma_s(n) sin(n a); Lambert-series / Ramanujan-Guinand type formula
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan's lost notebook p. 336; analysed and shown incorrect by B.C. Berndt, A. Dixit, A. Roy, A. Zaharescu (Adv. Math. 2017)

results.what: Laplace-transform consequence: Gamma(s+1/2){...sum sigma_s(n)[(x-in)^{-s-1/2}-(x+in)^{-s-1/2}]/(2i)} = (2 pi)^s{... + sqrt(pi) sum sigma_s(n) n^{-1/2} e^{-2 pi sqrt(2nx)} sin(pi/4 + 2 pi sqrt(2nx))}.
results.modern_name: Voronoi-type summation formula for sigma_s(n) (extended divisor problem), with Koshliakov/Kelvin-type kernel
results.usually_credited_to: Voronoi (1904) for the divisor-problem series. This specific (incorrect) form is Ramanujan's, corrected by Berndt-Dixit-Roy-Zaharescu (2017).

results.what: Integral: int_0^oo t^{-3/2} e^{-xt} sin(c/t) dt = sqrt(pi/c) e^{-sqrt(2cx)} sin(pi/4 + sqrt(2cx)).

deep.surprise_reason: This is page 336 of the lost notebook. It has already been published and analysed in detail by Berndt-Dixit-Roy-Zaharescu (2017), who showed both claims are vitiated by divergent series. The formal derivation is consistent but the claims are incorrect, so nothing new is attributed.

checkable.asserts: Kernel integral: int_0^oo t^(-3/2) e^(-xt) sin(c/t) dt = sqrt(pi/c) exp(-sqrt(2cx)) sin(pi/4+sqrt(2cx)), checked at x=1, c=2 (difference ~0).
Gamma(s+1/2)[(x-in)^(-s-1/2)-(x+in)^(-s-1/2)]/(2i) equals the Laplace transform of t^(s-1/2) sin(nt) (difference ~0).
The zeta(1-s) term transforms into (2 pi)^s zeta(1-s)/(2 sqrt(pi x)) (result 0).
The regularized constant term gives -(2 pi)^s 2 pi sqrt(pi x) zeta(-s) tan(pi s/2) (result 0, with sqrt(x) factored out).
The asymptotic size of the LHS series terms (times sigma_{-s}(n) >= 1) is not summable, so the left series diverges.
